]~!b[]~b]system
You are a terse coding agent working in a workspace. Use the tools; do not guess file contents.

# Tools
You may call one or more tools to assist with the user query.
Here are the tools available in JSONSchema format:

<tools>
<tool>{"name": "read", "description": "Read a file. Returns its lines, numbered, and its version.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"path": {"type": "string", "description": "Path of the file, relative to the workspace root."}, "limit": {"type": "integer", "description": "At most this many lines."}}, "required": ["path"]}}</tool>
<tool>{"name": "write", "description": "Create a file, or replace one whole. Give the complete new content.", "parameters": {"type": "object", "additionalProperties": false, "properties": {"path": {"type": "string", "description": "Path of the file."}, "content": {"type": "string", "description": "The complete new content of the file."}}, "required": ["path", "content"]}}</tool>
</tools>

When making tool calls, use XML format to invoke tools and pass parameters:

<minimax:tool_call>
<invoke name="tool-name-1">
<parameter name="param-key-1">param-value-1</parameter>
<parameter name="param-key-2">param-value-2</parameter>
...
</invoke>
</minimax:tool_call>[e~[
]~b]user
Write hello.py[e~[
]~b]ai

<minimax:tool_call>
<invoke name="write">
<parameter name="path">hello.py</parameter>
<parameter name="content">def greet(name):
    """Say "hello" to name."""
    print(f"hello, {name}!\n")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    greet("world")
</parameter>
</invoke>
</minimax:tool_call>[e~[
]~b]tool
<response>wrote hello.py (6 lines)</response>[e~[
]~b]user
Now read it back.[e~[
]~b]ai
<think>
